```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

FYI:
I did this analysis using this guide:
https://ngs101.com/how-to-build-gene-co-expression-networks-from-rna-seq-data-using-wgcna-complete-step-by-step-guide-for-absolute-beginners/
by Lei Guo, who also has tutorials available on youtube.
The source data used in this file is pulled from files previously created in the Differential Expression R markdown file.

```{r, libraries}
library(ggplot2) #pretty plots
library(ggrepel) #pretty plots with nice labels
library(WGCNA) #for wgcna
library(pheatmap) #for heatmaps
library(reshape2)
library(igraph)
library(STRINGdb)
library(tibble)
library(tidygraph) #for hubgene plot
library(ggraph) #for hubgene plot
library(purrr) #for chrom dist plot
```
```{r, Loading in Pre-processed RNA-seq Data}

#Loading normalized expression data
#Rows are genes, columns are samples
norm_counts <- read.csv("~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/normalized_counts.csv", header = TRUE)
rownames(norm_counts) <- NULL
norm_counts <- tibble::column_to_rownames(norm_counts, "Genes")

#Loading sample information
#Contains treatment/chromosome information for each sample
chicken_phenodata <- read.csv("~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/ChickenPhenodata_9ZW_2026.csv", sep = ";")
chicken_phenodata <- tibble::column_to_rownames(chicken_phenodata, "sample")
#relevel the chicken_phenodata columns
chicken_phenodata$Chromosome <- factor(chicken_phenodata$Chromosome, levels =c("ZZ", "ZW"))
chicken_phenodata$Treatment <- factor(chicken_phenodata$Treatment, levels =c("Saline", "Fadrozole"))
chicken_phenodata$Chromosome_Treatment <- factor(chicken_phenodata$Chromosome_Treatment, levels =c("SZZ", "SZW", "FZZ", "FZW"))
#Creating an abbreviated version for later use in figure making
chicken_phenodata_ab <- chicken_phenodata %>%
  rename(Chrom = Chromosome) %>%
  rename(Treat = Treatment) %>%
  mutate(Treat = case_when(
    Treat == "Fadrozole" ~ "Fad",
    Treat == "Saline" ~ "Sal",
    TRUE ~ Treat
  ))

#Loading gene annotation data
#Contains ensembl ids and gene symbols
gene_data <- read.table("~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/mart_result.tsv")

#Enable multi-threading for WGCNA
enableWGCNAThreads(nThreads = 8)
```


```{r, WGCNA Quality control and data filtering}

#Check for missing values
missing_count <- sum(is.na(norm_counts))
cat("Number of missing values:", missing_count, "\n")
#0 (7/28/26)

#Remove genes with missing values if any
if (missing_count > 0) {
  expr_data <- expr_data[complete.cases(expr_data), ]
  cat("Removed genes with missing values. New dimension:", dim(expr_data), "\n")
}

#Calculate variance for each gene
gene_variance <- apply(norm_counts, 1, var)

#I once had a plan to make all the figures using ggplot for consistency... this idea was quickly abandoned, but that's why some of these are done with ggplot instead of base r:

#Prepare data
var_log <- log10(gene_variance)
var_log <- var_log[is.finite(var_log)]
gene_variance_gg <- data.frame(var = var_log)
cutoff <- log10(quantile(gene_variance, 0.4, na.rm = TRUE))

gene_variance_distribution <- ggplot(gene_variance_gg, aes(x = var)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 50,
    fill = "lightblue",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    aes(xintercept = cutoff, color = "40th percentile cutoff"),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("40th percentile cutoff" = "red")) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Gene Variance (log10)",
    x = "log10(Variance)",
    y = "Frequency",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.98, 0.98),
    legend.justification = c(1, 1),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    legend.key = element_blank()
  )
#Check plot before saving
show(gene_variance_distribution)
#Save
ggsave(
  "~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/WGCNA/WGCNA_Plots/Gene_Variance_Distribution.png",
  plot = gene_variance_distribution,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 100
)

#Remove genes with very low variance (bottom 40%)
#(These genes provide little information for co-expression analysis)
variance_threshold <- quantile(gene_variance, 0.4)
cat("Variance threshold (40th percentile):", variance_threshold, "\n")
#0.01505024 (7/28/26)
 
norm_counts_filtered <- norm_counts[gene_variance > variance_threshold, ]
cat("Genes after variance filtering:", nrow(norm_counts_filtered), "\n")
#14706 (7/28/26)
 
#Transpose for WGCNA (samples as rows, genes as columns)
expr_matrix <- t(norm_counts_filtered)
 
#Check sample clustering to identify outliers
sample_tree <- hclust(dist(expr_matrix), method = "average")
png("~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/WGCNA/WGCNA_Plots/Sample_Clustering_Outliers.png", width = 1200, height = 600, res = 100)
par(mar = c(2, 5, 2, 2))
plot(sample_tree, 
     main = "Sample Clustering to Detect Outliers",
     sub = "Height represents dissimilarity between samples",
     xlab = "", 
     cex = 0.7)
abline(h = 200, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
dev.off()
```

```{r, WGCNA Prepare trait data matrix}

#Create binary trait matrix for each experimental condition
#Each column represents presence (1) or absence (0) of that condition
trait_data <- data.frame(
  Fadrozole = as.numeric(chicken_phenodata$Treatment == "Fadrozole"),
  Saline = as.numeric(chicken_phenodata$Treatment == "Saline"),
  ZW = as.numeric(chicken_phenodata$Chromosome == "ZW"),
  ZZ = as.numeric(chicken_phenodata$Chromosome == "ZZ")
)
#Set row names to match expression matrix
rownames(trait_data) <- rownames(expr_matrix)
#Verify that sample names match between expression and trait data
if (!all(rownames(expr_matrix) == rownames(trait_data))) {
  stop("ERROR: Sample names don't match between expression and trait data!")
}

#Creating the trait data matrix for looking at specific interactions
trait_data_int <- binarizeCategoricalColumns(chicken_phenodata$Chromosome_Treatment, includePairwise = TRUE, includeLevelVsAll = FALSE, minCount = 1)
#Reordering the columns for more intuitive reading
trait_data_int <- trait_data_int[,c(
  "data.SZW.vs.SZZ",
  "data.FZW.vs.FZZ",
  "data.FZZ.vs.SZZ",
  "data.FZW.vs.SZW",
  "data.FZZ.vs.SZW",
  "data.FZW.vs.SZZ" 
)]
#Renaming the columns for more intuitive reading
colnames(trait_data_int) <- c(
  "SZZ vs SZW",
  "FZZ vs FZW",
  "SZZ vs FZZ",
  "SZW vs FZW",
  "SZW vs FZZ",
  "SZZ vs FZW"
)
#Set row names to match expression matrix
rownames(trait_data_int) <- colnames(norm_counts)
#Verify that sample names match between expression and trait data
if (!all(colnames(norm_counts) == rownames(trait_data_int))) {
  stop("ERROR: Sample names don't match between expression and trait data!")
}
```

```{r, Choosing Soft-Thresholding Power}

#Calculate network topology for various soft-thresholding powers
powers <- c(seq(1, 10, by = 1), seq(12, 20, by = 2))
 
#This function tests different power values
sft <- pickSoftThreshold(
  expr_matrix,
  powerVector = powers,
  networkType = "signed",
  verbose = 3,
  randomSeed = 4444 # (7/28/26) setting a seed so we get consistent modules to use in analysis
)
 
#Plot scale-free topology fit index as a function of power
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
 
#Scale-free topology fit
png("~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/WGCNA/WGCNA_Plots/Soft_Thresholding_Power_Selection.png", width = 1200, height = 600, res = 100)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
 
#Scale-free topology fit
plot(sft$fitIndices[, 1],
     -sign(sft$fitIndices[, 3]) * sft$fitIndices[, 2],
     xlab = "Soft Threshold (power)",
     ylab = "Scale Free Topology Model Fit, signed R^2",
     main = "Scale Independence",
     type = "n")
text(sft$fitIndices[, 1],
     -sign(sft$fitIndices[, 3]) * sft$fitIndices[, 2],
     labels = powers, 
     cex = 0.9, 
     col = "red")
abline(h = 0.85, col = "red", lty = 2)
 
#Mean connectivity
plot(sft$fitIndices[, 1],
     sft$fitIndices[, 5],
     xlab = "Soft Threshold (power)",
     ylab = "Mean Connectivity",
     main = "Mean Connectivity",
     type = "n")
text(sft$fitIndices[, 1],
     sft$fitIndices[, 5],
     labels = powers, 
     cex = 0.9, 
     col = "red")
 
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
dev.off()
 
#Choose the power: first value that reaches plateau in scale-free topology and gives reasonable mean connectivity
soft_power <- sft$powerEstimate
if (is.na(soft_power)) {
  soft_power <- 6  # Use 6 as default if automatic selection fails
  cat("Warning: Automatic power selection failed. Using default power =", soft_power, "\n")
} else {
  cat("Selected soft-thresholding power:", soft_power, "\n")
}
#14 (3/13/26), 12 (7/28/26)

```

```{r, Construct Network and Identify Modules}

#CRITICAL: Fix for WGCNA cor() function bug
#WGCNA has its own cor() function that conflicts with stats::cor()
cor <- WGCNA::cor
 
#Setting a seed for consistent results
#set.seed(4444)
#One-step network construction and module detection
net <- blockwiseModules(
  expr_matrix,
  power = soft_power,
  networkType = "signed",
  TOMType = "signed",
  minModuleSize = 30,
  reassignThreshold = 0,
  mergeCutHeight = 0.25,
  numericLabels = TRUE,
  pamRespectsDendro = FALSE,
  saveTOMs = TRUE,
  saveTOMFileBase = "Chicken_TOM",
  verbose = 3, 
  randomSeed = 4444 # (7/28/26) setting a seed so we get consistent modules to use in analysis
)
 
#Restore the standard cor() function after network construction
cor <- stats::cor
 
#Convert numeric module labels to colors for visualization
module_colors <- labels2colors(net$colors)
 
#Count genes in each module
module_table <- table(module_colors)
cat("\nNumber of modules identified:", length(unique(module_colors)) - 1, "\n")
#Number of modules identified: 25 (3/11/26), 23 (7/28/26)
print(module_table)
#black blue brown cyan
#580   1578 1411  300
 
#Plot the dendrogram with module colors
png("~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/WGCNA/WGCNA_Plots/Gene_Dendrogram_Modules.png", width = 1200, height = 800, res = 100)
plotDendroAndColors(
  net$dendrograms[[1]],
  module_colors[net$blockGenes[[1]]],
  "Module colors",
  dendroLabels = FALSE,
  hang = 0.03,
  addGuide = TRUE,
  guideHang = 0.05,
  main = "Gene Dendrogram and Module Colors"
)
dev.off()
```

```{r, Calculate and Visualize Module Eigengenes}

#Extract module eigengenes
module_eigengenes <- net$MEs

#Making the modules named by color
module_eigengenes <- moduleEigengenes(expr_matrix, module_colors)$eigengenes

#Reorder modules by hierarchical clustering of eigengenes
module_eigengenes <- orderMEs(module_eigengenes)
 
#Visualize module eigengenes across samples
#Create a heatmap showing how each module's expression varies across samples
png("~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/WGCNA/WGCNA_Plots/Module_Eigengenes_Heatmap.png", width = 1200, height = 1000, res = 100)
pheatmap(
  t(module_eigengenes),
  scale = "row",
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
  clustering_method = "average",
  annotation_col = trait_data,
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  main = "Module Eigengenes Across Samples",
  color = colorRampPalette(c("#1F1BB3", "white", "#D41159"))(50),
  fontsize = 8
)
dev.off()
```

```{r, Module Eigengene Network}

#Calculate correlation between module eigengenes
me_correlation <- cor(module_eigengenes, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
 
#Calculate p-values
me_pvalue <- corPvalueStudent(me_correlation, nSamples)
 
#Create adjacency matrix: keep correlations > 0.5 and p < 0.05
me_adjacency <- (abs(me_correlation) > 0.5) & (me_pvalue < 0.05)
diag(me_adjacency) <- FALSE  # Remove self-connections
 
#Check if there are any edges
n_edges <- sum(me_adjacency) / 2
cat("\nNumber of module pairs with |correlation| > 0.5 and p < 0.05:", n_edges, "\n")
#Number of module pairs with |correlation| > 0.5 and p < 0.05: 56 (7/25/26) 
 
if (n_edges == 0) {
  cat("\nNo strong correlations between modules at |r| > 0.5.\n")
  cat("Trying |r| > 0.3...\n\n")
  me_adjacency <- (abs(me_correlation) > 0.3) & (me_pvalue < 0.05)
  diag(me_adjacency) <- FALSE
  n_edges <- sum(me_adjacency) / 2
  correlation_threshold <- 0.3
} else {
  correlation_threshold <- 0.5
}
 
if (n_edges == 0) {
  cat("No significant correlations between modules even at |r| > 0.3.\n")
  cat("Modules are largely independent.\n")
} else {
  #Create network of module relationships
  me_network <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
    me_adjacency,
    mode = "undirected"
  )
}
 
  #Convert numeric module labels to color names
  #module_names_numeric <- gsub("ME", "", names(module_eigengenes))
  #module_names_colors <- labels2colors(as.numeric(module_names_numeric))
  
  #Plain module color names without ME (altered from source code because we changed the module names to colors previously for a nicer correlation map)
  module_names_colors <- gsub("ME", "", names(module_eigengenes))
 
  #cat("Module numeric labels:", head(module_names_numeric), "\n")
  cat("Corresponding colors:", head(module_names_colors), "\n")
 
  #Set vertex colors using the actual color names
  V(me_network)$color <- module_names_colors
 
  #Calculate node sizes based on module size
  #Use color names to get counts from module_colors table
  module_sizes_table <- table(module_colors)
  module_sizes_net <- module_sizes_table[module_names_colors]
 
  #Handle any missing values (modules with no genes)
  module_sizes_net[is.na(module_sizes_net)] <- 10
 
  node_sizes_me <- log10(as.numeric(module_sizes_net) + 1) * 10 + 10
 
  #Plot module network
if (n_edges > 0) {
  png("~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/WGCNA/WGCNA_Plots/Module_Eigengene_Network.png", width = 1000, height = 1000, res = 100)
  par(mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
  set.seed(123)
  plot(me_network,
       vertex.size = node_sizes_me,
       vertex.label = module_names_colors,
       vertex.label.cex = 0.7,
       vertex.label.color = "black",
       vertex.color = module_names_colors,
       vertex.frame.color = "black",
       edge.width = 3,
       edge.color = "gray40",
       layout = layout_with_fr(me_network),
       main = paste0("Module Eigengene Network\n(|correlation| > ", 
                     correlation_threshold, ", p < 0.05)"))
  dev.off()
}
 
 
#Also show a correlation heatmap for reference
#Use color names for row/column labels
me_cor_labeled <- me_correlation
rownames(me_cor_labeled) <- module_names_colors
colnames(me_cor_labeled) <- module_names_colors

png("~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/WGCNA/WGCNA_Plots/Module_Eigengene_Correlation_Heatmap.png", width = 1200, height = 1200, res = 100)
pheatmap(
  me_cor_labeled,
  color = colorRampPalette(c("#1F1BB3", "white", "#D41159"))(50),
  breaks = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 51),
  clustering_distance_rows = "correlation",
  clustering_distance_cols = "correlation",
  main = "Module Eigengene Correlation Heatmap",
  fontsize = 7
)
dev.off()
```

```{r, Module Membership Information}

#Extracting kME (module eigengene connectivity) values for each gene in relation to each module
module_kMEs <- cor(expr_matrix, module_eigengenes, use = "p")

#Creating matrix which contains the kME values only for the genes part of each respective module
membership_matrix <- module_kMEs
module_numbers <- substring(colnames(membership_matrix), 3) #Removes ME from module names
colnames(membership_matrix) <- module_numbers
#Function to replace kME values for non corresponding genes and modules with NA
for (i in seq_along(module_numbers)) {
  membership_matrix[module_colors != module_numbers[i], i] <- NA}
#Save as csv file
write.csv(membership_matrix, "~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/WGCNA/WGCNA_Tables/Module_Membership_kME.csv")

#Making a table with the gene membership for each module
module_gene_lists <- split(names(module_colors), module_colors)
max_len <- max(lengths(module_gene_lists))

module_membership <- data.frame(
  lapply(module_gene_lists, function(x) c(x, rep(NA, max_len - length(x)))))
#Save as csv file
write.csv(module_membership, "~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/WGCNA/WGCNA_Tables/Module_Membership.csv")
```

```{r, Mean & Distribution of Module Eigengenes by Sample}

#Create sample info with correct levels to be used
sample_info <- chicken_phenodata_ab %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Sample") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Chrom = factor(Chrom, levels = c("ZZ", "ZW")),
    Treat = factor(Treat, levels = c("Sal", "Fad"))
  )

#Creating a data frame with module eigengene info for each sample
ME_long <- module_eigengenes %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("Sample") %>%
  select(-MEgrey) %>% #Taking out grey module because it is unassigned genes
  left_join(
    sample_info %>% select(Sample, Treat, Chrom, Chromosome_Treatment),
    by = "Sample"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("ME"),
    names_to = "Module",
    values_to = "Eigengene"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Module = sub("^ME", "", Module))

#Function to make text light or dark based on background luminance (gamma corrected)
text_color <- function(bg, cutoff = 0.2) {
  rgb <- col2rgb(bg) / 255
  rgb <- ifelse(rgb <= 0.03928, rgb/12.92, ((rgb+0.055)/1.055)^2.4)
  luminance <- 0.2126 * rgb[1,] + 0.7152 * rgb[2,] + 0.0722 * rgb[3,]
  ifelse(luminance < cutoff, "white", "black")
}

#Manually assigning colors to each module color so the headers can have corresponding colors
module_colors_ME <- c("black","blue","brown","cyan","darkgreen","darkred","darkturquoise","green","greenyellow","grey60","lightcyan","lightgreen","lightyellow", "magenta","midnightblue","pink","purple", "red","royalblue","salmon","tan","turquoise","yellow")
names(module_colors_ME) <- module_colors_ME
fills <- module_colors_ME
text_cols <- text_color(fills)
rep_len_list <- function(x, n) rep(list(x), length(fills))

#Making plot
MEplot <- ggplot(
  ME_long,aes(x = Treat, y = Eigengene, color = Chrom, group = Chrom)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line") +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.1) +
  ggh4x::facet_wrap2(
    ~Module,
    ncol = 8,
    scales = "fixed",
    strip = ggh4x::strip_themed(
      background_x = ggh4x::elem_list_rect(fill = fills),
      text_x = ggh4x::elem_list_text(
        color = text_cols,
        size = rep(8, length(fills)),
        margin = rep_len_list(
          ggplot2::margin(2, 2, 2, 2),
          length(fills))))) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(ZZ = "#FCA636", ZW = "#B12A90")) +
  labs(x = "Treatment") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    # legend.position = "inside",
    # legend.position.inside = c(0.9, 0.1),
    # legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black"),
    # legend.key = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    # legend.key.size = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    # legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    # legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.position = "none", #for the purpose of making pretty figures the legend has been removed, but the code for it is above
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "black")
```

```{r, Hub Gene Network/Coexpression}
##Gather neccesary data

#Directory to save everything to
out_dir <- "~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/WGCNA"

#Need to assign module names
names(module_colors) <- colnames(expr_matrix)

#Top 1000 most variable genes
top_genes_var <- names(sort(apply(expr_matrix, 2, var), decreasing = TRUE))[1:1000]

#TOM on the subset
tom_subset <- TOMsimilarity(
  adjacency(expr_matrix[, top_genes_var], power = soft_power, type = "signed")
)
dimnames(tom_subset) <- list(top_genes_var, top_genes_var)

#Helper: threshold TOM -> igraph object with module colors attached
build_network <- function(tom, cutoff) {
  tom[tom < cutoff] <- 0
  g <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(tom, mode = "undirected",
                                   weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE)
  V(g)$color <- module_colors[V(g)$name]
  V(g)$color[is.na(V(g)$color)] <- "grey"
  g
}

##Network Visualization (base igraph, top 5% of connections)
tom_threshold <- quantile(tom_subset[upper.tri(tom_subset)], 0.95)
cat("TOM threshold (95th percentile):", tom_threshold, "\n")

network_graph <- build_network(tom_subset, tom_threshold)
node_sizes    <- log10(degree(network_graph) + 1) * 3 + 3

#Save as png file
png(file.path(out_dir, "WGCNA_Plots/Coexpression_Network.png"),
    width = 1200, height = 1200, res = 100)
par(mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
set.seed(123)
plot(network_graph,
     vertex.size = node_sizes,
     vertex.label = NA,
     vertex.color = V(network_graph)$color,
     vertex.frame.color = NA,
     edge.width = 0.5,
     edge.color = "gray80",
     layout = layout_with_fr(network_graph),
     main = "Co-expression Network\n(Top 1000 Variable Genes, Top 5% Connections)")

legend_cols <- setdiff(unique(V(network_graph)$color), "grey")
if (length(legend_cols) <= 10) {
  legend("topright", legend = legend_cols, col = legend_cols,
         pch = 19, cex = 0.7, title = "Modules", bty = "n")}
dev.off()

##Save the top 10 hub genes per module into a csv file
top_n <- 10

#Gene-name table
module_gene_lists <- split(names(module_colors), module_colors)
max_len <- max(lengths(module_gene_lists))
module_gene_table <- data.frame(
  lapply(module_gene_lists, function(x) c(x, rep(NA, max_len - length(x)))))

#Rebuild kME, correlation of each gene with each module eigengene
module_membership <- cor(expr_matrix, module_eigengenes, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

hub_gene_table <- as.data.frame(sapply(unique(module_colors), function(mod) {
  genes <- names(module_colors)[module_colors == mod]
  kme   <- module_membership[genes, paste0("ME", mod)]
  hubs  <- names(sort(kme, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(top_n, length(kme)))]
  c(hubs, rep(NA, top_n - length(hubs)))
}))

#Create csv
write.csv(hub_gene_table, file.path(out_dir, "WGCNA_Tables/Hub_Genes_Table.csv"))

library(tidygraph)
##Co-expression plot for Illustrator (ggraph, edges with TOM >= 0.05)
graph_tbl <- as_tbl_graph(build_network(tom_subset, 0.05)) %>%
  mutate(size = centrality_degree(weights = weight))

coexpression_plot <- ggraph(graph_tbl, layout = "fr", niter = 5000) +
  geom_edge_link(alpha = 0.05, color = "grey") +
  geom_node_point(aes(color = I(color), size = size)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.5, 5), name = "Connectivity") +
  guides(size = guide_legend(direction = "horizontal", title.position = "top",
                             label.position = "bottom", nrow = 1)) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        legend.text  = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"))
show(coexpression_plot)
#Save as pdf
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "WGCNA_Plots/Co-expression_plot.pdf"),
       coexpression_plot, width = 2.5, height = 3)
```

```{r, Chromosomal Distribution of Genes by Module}

##Gathering information needed

#Chromosome of each gene
gene_chrom <- gene_data %>%
  select(gene = symbols_ids, chr = chromosome_name)

#Find distribution across each module
module_chrom_list <- map(colnames(membership_matrix), function(mod) {
  
  #Get genes in this module
  genes_in_module <- rownames(membership_matrix)[
    !is.na(membership_matrix[, mod])
  ]
  
  #Subset chromosome data
  chrom_subset <- gene_chrom %>%
    filter(gene %in% genes_in_module)
  
  #Count chromosomes
  chrom_counts <- chrom_subset %>%
    count(chr, name = "Freq") %>%
    rename(Var1 = chr)
  
  list(chrom_counts = chrom_counts)
})

#Name the list
names(module_chrom_list) <- colnames(membership_matrix)

#Chromosome classification function
classify_chrom <- function(chr) {
  autosomes <- c("KZ626819.1","AADN05001218.1", as.character(1:38)) #These are genomic accession numbers for loci known to be on autosomes
  z_chroms  <- c("Z", "AADN05001439.1")
  w_chroms  <- c("W")
  mitochondrial <- c("MT")
  case_when(
    chr %in% autosomes ~ "Autosomes",
    chr %in% z_chroms  ~ "Z Chromosome",
    chr %in% w_chroms  ~ "W Chromosome",
    chr %in% mitochondrial ~ "Mitochondria",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_   #Everything else ignored
  )}

#Define chromosomal categories
categories <- c("Autosomes", "Z Chromosome", "W Chromosome", "Mitochondria")

#Getting chrom data from each module
chrom_list <- lapply(module_chrom_list, function(x) x$chrom_counts)

#Run function on all consistently
module_chrom_sums <- map(chrom_list, ~{
  .x %>%
    mutate(category = classify_chrom(Var1)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(category)) %>%
    group_by(category) %>%
    summarise(total_genes = sum(Freq), .groups = "drop")%>%
    complete(category = categories, fill = list(total_genes = 0))
})

#Collecting information in one place
module_chrom_stats <- bind_rows(module_chrom_sums, .id = "module") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = module, values_from = total_genes) %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("category") %>%
  as.matrix()

#Shifting configuration for barplot
module_chrom_df <- as.data.frame(module_chrom_stats) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("category") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -category,
    names_to = "module",
    values_to = "total_genes"
  )

#Relevel so it's in the order I want
module_chrom_df$category <- factor(
  module_chrom_df$category,
  levels = c("W Chromosome", "Z Chromosome", "Mitochondria", "Autosomes")
)

#Save as a pdf for export to illustrator
pdf("~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/WGCNA/WGCNA_Plots/Module_Chromosome_Distribution.pdf", width = 4.5, height = 2.25)
par(ps = 8) #mar = c(4, 3.5, 1, .25), ps = 8) 
ggplot(module_chrom_df, aes(x = module, y = total_genes, fill = category)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Autosomes" = "#A4CE4C",
               "Mitochondria" = "yellow",
               "Z Chromosome" = "#FCA636",
               "W Chromosome" = "#B12A90FF")) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Total Genes",
    fill = NULL) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1, color = "black", size = 8),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none")
dev.off()
```
